headline: POP3 RETR and TOP dot-stuff a stored body against the CRLF endings a client parses
summary: `b.mail.server.pop3` built its `RETR` and `TOP` multiline responses by dot-stuffing the stored message bytes with `b.safeSmtp.dotStuff`, which doubles a line-initial `.` only where the preceding line ended in a canonical CRLF. A message stored with bare-LF or bare-CR line endings, the form a Maildir or mbox maildrop keeps, therefore emitted any line consisting of a single `.` un-stuffed. A client that treats a bare LF or CR as a line boundary reads that `.` as the end of the message and the bytes after it as unrequested response lines, truncating the message and letting a sender who mails such a body smuggle content into the client stream. `RETR` and `TOP` now canonicalize the body to CRLF before dot-stuffing through the new `b.safeSmtp.dotStuffForWire`, so every line ending is CRLF and every line-initial `.` is doubled.

items.title: POP3 RETR/TOP dot-stuff a stored body against the line endings a client parses
items.body: A POP3 server transmits a message as CRLF-terminated lines and byte-stuffs any line beginning with the termination octet `.` (RFC 1939 §3). `b.mail.server.pop3` dot-stuffed the stored bytes with `b.safeSmtp.dotStuff`, which stuffs a line-initial `.` only where the preceding line ended in a canonical CRLF. A body stored with bare-LF or bare-CR line endings, the common Maildir and mbox form, left a line consisting of a lone `.` un-stuffed, so the RETR or TOP response carried a `.` line at a non-canonical boundary. A client that splits lines on a bare LF or CR, as several do for historical POP3 and mbox compatibility, reads that line as the end-of-message terminator: it truncates the message and parses everything the server sends after it as further response lines. This is the retrieval-side analog of the SMTP DATA-body smuggling refused in 0.20.8. RETR and TOP now canonicalize the body to CRLF before dot-stuffing, so the response is well-formed and every line-initial `.` is doubled. STAT, LIST, and RETR report the canonical wire octet count the `mailStore` provides for a message, and RETR delivers a body of exactly that size, so the advertised sizes are consistent across the three commands; a backend that stores messages with bare-LF endings reports the CRLF size, not the stored byte length.

items.title: `b.safeSmtp.dotStuffForWire` canonicalizes line endings before dot-stuffing
items.body: `b.safeSmtp.dotStuffForWire(buf)` canonicalizes every line ending in a message body to CRLF and then applies RFC 5321 §4.5.2 / RFC 1939 §3 dot-stuffing. `b.safeSmtp.dotStuff` on its own stuffs a line-initial `.` only at a canonical CRLF boundary and documents that its caller must canonicalize or refuse bare-LF first; this primitive composes that canonicalization with the stuffing, for a caller serving a stored body over the wire such as a POP3 RETR or TOP response.

items.title: `b.safeSmtp.canonicalizeEol` rewrites line endings to CRLF
items.body: `b.safeSmtp.canonicalizeEol(buf)` rewrites every line ending in a buffer to canonical CRLF: a bare LF and a bare CR each become CRLF, an existing CRLF is unchanged. It brings a stored message body to the wire form a POP3 or SMTP multiline response requires before dot-stuffing, and gives the octet count the peer receives.
